# Incident Report — MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis

## Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.21.58** |
| MAC | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (also broadcasts NetBIOS name **WIN11OFFICE**, AD domain **win11office.com**) |
| Logged-in user | **gwyatt** (confirmed via Kerberos `CNameString` exchanges between 10.1.21.58 and the domain controller 10.1.21.2) |

Local subnet is 10.1.21.0/24; DC/gateway peer is 10.1.21.2 (MAC 14:b3:1f:2d:ce:69). NBNS/DHCP/ARP all agree on the IP-MAC-hostname binding above (a self-assigned APIPA address 169.254.227.202 also broadcasts the same NetBIOS names, same MAC — same host, transient interface).

## Malware Family

**Attribution is behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No IDS/Suricata alert export was provided with this evidence — only the raw pcap — so there is no signature match to cite.

Behavior observed: a chain of disposable, cheap-TLD "file hosting" domains (`.sbs`, `.lat`, `.cyou`, `.su`, `.cc`) delivers a browser-fingerprinting gate page, which profiles the victim's browser (User-Agent, WebGL/canvas fingerprint, hardware concurrency) and POSTs the profile back to a controller before serving a **password/name-protected ZIP payload** (server error string `cant open archive 172.56.88.98-038485b1855ec7a1ba5bbda042ad17a1.zip` was returned to the victim, confirming a gated archive-delivery step keyed to the visitor). This is the signature workflow of a **pay-per-install / fake-download malvertising loader chain** (the "file hub" naming mimics MediaFire/MegaFile-style download sites). The payload itself is TLS-encrypted in transit, so the actual dropped executable's identity/hash cannot be recovered from this capture. Treat the family as an unidentified loader/stealer delivered via this gate — do not name a specific strain without the decrypted payload or an IDS match.

## Infection / Traffic Timeline

| t (rel, sec) | Event |
|---|---|
| ~45.3 | DNS query + TCP/TLS to `hiyter.com` → 104.21.22.231, 172.67.207.145 (entry redirector) |
| ~45.8–46.0 | DNS + TLS to `media.megafilehub4.lat` → 104.21.48.156, 172.67.154.67 (fake-download landing) |
| ~48.3 | DNS + TLS to `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` → 104.21.46.67, 172.67.136.13 — **16 MB inbound to victim**, the largest single transfer in the capture (candidate payload delivery, TLS-encrypted, content not recoverable) |
| ~90.3–90.5 | DNS + TLS to `whooptm.cyou` → 62.72.32.156 |
| ~92.3–103.8 | Repeated cleartext HTTP (port 80) and TLS (port 443, 14+ separate sessions) to **`whitepepper.su` → 153.92.1.49** — fingerprinting/checkin controller, see below |
| ~122.8 | DNS + TLS to `holiday-forever.cc` → 80.97.160.24 |
| ~126.5 | DNS + TLS to `communicationfirewall-security.cc` → 104.21.9.36, 172.67.141.109 |

## whitepepper.su Checkin Traffic (cleartext, fully observed)

```
GET  http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome
POST http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?...&agent=Chrome&act=log
GET  http://whitepepper.su/favicon.ico
GET  http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?...&agent=Edge
POST http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?...&agent=Edge&act=log
GET  http://whitepepper.su/favicon.ico
```
The GET returns a JavaScript fingerprinting page that collects `navigator` properties, WebGL renderer/vendor, and a canvas-fingerprint payload, then POSTs it back via `act=log`. The site re-runs this cycle for both "Chrome" and "Edge" agent identifiers and repeats connections on port 443 well beyond this window (14 distinct TLS sessions observed), consistent with a persistent controller checkin rather than a one-shot landing page.

## Indicators of Compromise (all grounded in this capture)

**C2 / malicious endpoints (IP:port):**
- 153.92.1.49:80, 153.92.1.49:443 — `whitepepper.su`, fingerprinting/checkin controller (repeated beaconing)
- 104.21.46.67:443, 172.67.136.13:443 — `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`, largest transfer (16 MB), likely payload stage
- 104.21.48.156:443, 172.67.154.67:443 — `media.megafilehub4.lat`
- 104.21.22.231:443, 172.67.207.145:443 — `hiyter.com`
- 62.72.32.156:443 — `whooptm.cyou`
- 80.97.160.24:443 — `holiday-forever.cc`
- 104.21.9.36:443, 172.67.141.109:443 — `communicationfirewall-security.cc`

**Malicious domains:**
- hiyter.com
- media.megafilehub4.lat
- arch.filemegahab4.sbs
- whooptm.cyou
- whitepepper.su
- holiday-forever.cc
- communicationfirewall-security.cc

**URLs (cleartext, directly observed):**
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log`

- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log`

**Content transferred (SHA256, extracted directly from the HTTP objects in this pcap):**
| Object | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| fingerprinting JS page (`set_agent...agent=Chrome`) | a1ee2e3055dc4ce0d60eb6c2c8a655e705b3607bd33d65794e67adf22a2a0124 |
| fingerprinting JS page (`set_agent...agent=Edge`) | 8f97a4018d4b0675b9592660394cf5b73f1be2252e27aff64a8f160af9079f46 |
| checkin log POST body (Chrome, `act=log`) | 713757395cb4bdc2f6786551ee10a32d465b53315fed9a4a1e03b8053506daf0 |
| checkin log POST body (Edge, `act=log`) | 2049fb3664b6b96eb36623732dfc5a01de8bc1f73e1adf5be6645b872cfd5063 |
| gate-error response ("cant open archive 172.56.88.98-038485b1855ec7a1ba5bbda042ad17a1.zip") | c520a471ca6dfd70251b066fd87b5699a623d04e4da7526b2e1d97af158ccd10 |
| favicon.ico (whitepepper.su) | 74ab801591b951bcb6b248a8ef9321388a45ecf8badd2893aea4aa360b26ea90 |

**Referenced-but-not-transferred artifact:** the server error string names an archive `172.56.88.98-038485b1855ec7a1ba5bbda042ad17a1.zip` (visitor-IP-keyed filename) — this confirms a gated payload-delivery mechanism but the archive itself was never observed transferred in this capture (it TLS-encrypts or was withheld for this session's fingerprint).

**Benign context (not IOCs, listed to distinguish from noise):** Microsoft/Google telemetry and update traffic (`msftconnecttest.com`, `clients2.google.com` Omaha updater, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `windows.msn.com`, MS/Google safebrowsing, mDNS/SSDP/LLMNR local discovery, DHCP/NBNS/ARP host discovery) — all normal Windows 11 / Office / Chrome background chatter, unrelated to the incident.

**Note on AD/DCE-RPC volume:** heavy SAMR/LSARPC traffic (1,500+ paired requests) between 10.1.21.58 and the DC 10.1.21.2 occurs in the same 20–131s window as the malicious contacts. This is elevated relative to typical background chatter and worth flagging for follow-up, but without decrypted payload or an IDS match it cannot be confidently tied to attacker enumeration versus normal Group Policy/logon processing — reported as an observation, not a confirmed IOC.
